newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli entrepreneur Shoul Eisenberg dies.
newsitem.headline: Israeli entrepreneur Shoul Eisenberg dies.

text.p: Israeli industrialist Shoul Eisenberg died on Thursday in Beijing, his family said. He was 76.
Eisenberg died of an apparent heart attack, a family representative said.
The Munich-born Eisenberg fled Nazi Germany in 1938, eventually settling in Japan, where he founded companies that after World War Two supplied raw materials to Japanese steel industries.
Eisenberg expanded his operations to include a wide range of industrial concerns in Asia, South America, Europe, and Israel, to which he moved his family in the 1960s.
He took a particularly active role in trading and investing in China, and was widely regarded for many years as an intermediary between the People's Republic and Israel.
Eisenberg's interests in Israel were centred on Israel Corporation, which controls Israel Chemicals, the Zim Israel Navigation shipping line, and Oil Refineries Ltd.
He is survived by his widow, Lea, five daughters, and a son, Erwin, who in recent years has assumed key roles in a number of Eisenberg's companies.
